slides.title: Remote Logging
slides.body:
What is a Port ?
Think of an IP address as an apartment building address, and a Port number as the flat number inside, It tells the data which application's door to knock on

slides.title: Remote Logging
slides.body:
What is Telnet?
TELNET stands for TELecommunication NETwork (also called Terminal Network). It is an application-layer protocol used for remote login over a TCP/IP network. It uses TCP Port 23, Developed in 1969, one of the oldest internet protocols
Input from clientKeyboard to server
Output from ServerTo client display

slides.title: Remote Logging
slides.body:
What is NVT?
NVT (Network Virtual Terminal) is a virtual device that acts as a translator between different types of real terminals
Since different computers may use different character sets, NVT provides a common standard format so that any machine can communicate with any other machine, regardless of their operating system
NVT (Network Virtual Terminal)

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
How Does Telnet Work?
User types characters on the local machine
Telnet Client converts characters into NVT (Network Virtual Terminal) format 
NVT-formatted characters travel through the Internet via TCP Port 23

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
How Does Telnet Work?
Telnet Server on the remote machine converts NVT characters back into a format the remote OS understands
Remote OS executes the command and sends the output back through the same path

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
User Journey (4 - Step Process)

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
Why is Telnet Insecure?
Telnet transmits all data in plain text including usernames and passwords
No encryption: data travels through the network as readable text
No authentication mechanism: does not verify the identity of the server
Problem

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
Why is Telnet Insecure?
Anyone on the network between the client and server can intercept and read the data using a packet sniffer (like Wireshark)
Vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attacks
Vulnerable to eavesdropping and credential theft
Consequence

slides.title: Telnet
slides.body:
Why is Telnet Insecure?
Because of these security flaws, telnet has been largely replaced by SSH for remote access in modern networks. Telnet is still used in some legacy systems and for local network testing

slides.title: Remote Logging
slides.body:
What is SSH (Secure Shell) ?
SSH stands for Secure Shell
It is a cryptographic network protocol for secure remote login and command execution over an unsecured network
It uses TCP Port 22
Created in 1995 by Tatu Ylönen as a secure replacement for Telnet
Current version: SSH-2 (standardized by IETF)

slides.title: SSH (Secure Shell)
slides.body:
How Does SSH Work ?
Three Security Pillars 
Message Type
Direction
Lock
Encryption
Purpose
All data (including passwords, commands, output) is encrypted using algorithms like AES, so even if intercepted, it cannot be read
Shield
Authentication
SSH verifies identity of both the server and the user. Supports password-based and public key-based authentication

slides.title: SSH (Secure Shell)
slides.body:
How Does SSH Work ?
Message Type
Direction
Checkmark
Data Integrity
Purpose
Uses hashing (SHA, MD5) to ensure data is not tampered with during transmission

slides.title: SSH (Secure Shell)
slides.body:
SSH Architecture
Transport Layer
TCP/IP Connection, Encryption, Compression, Integrity Checks, Key Exchange
User Authentication Layer
Password, Public Key, Host-based
Connection Layer
Multiple Logical Channels, Shell, SCP, SFTP, Port Forwarding
Client
Server
SSH Session

slides.title: SSH (Secure Shell)
slides.body:
SSH Authentication Methods
Password-Based
User enters a username and password, Unlike Telnet, the password is encrypted before being sent over the network, Simple to use, but weak passwords can still be guessed

slides.title: SSH (Secure Shell)
slides.body:
SSH Authentication Methods
Key-Based (Public Key)
User generates a key pair a Public Key (kept on server) and a Private Key (kept on user's machine), Only the matching pair can establish a connection, More secure, no password travels over the network at all

slides.title: SSH Authentication Methods
slides.body:
Analogy
 Password-based is like entering a building by telling the guard a secret code, secure, but someone could overhear it, Key-based is like using a unique fingerprint scanner, only your fingerprint works, and you can't copy it

slides.title: Telnet and SSH
slides.body:
Key Insight
SSH has almost entirely replaced Telnet in modern networks
The only reason Telnet still exists is for backward compatibility with very old (legacy) devices that don't support SSH
In interviews and exams, always emphasize that Telnet sends data in plain text, while SSH encrypts everything

What is Network Management ?
Network management refers to the process of monitoring, maintaining, and optimizing a network to ensure its efficient and secure operation.

What is SNMP?
SNMP stands for Simple Network Management Protocol
SNMP is an application-layer protocol for monitoring and managing network devices

Routers
Switches

Servers
IoT devices
Check link status, bandwidth usage

Track rules, traffic, CPU load 
Monitor memory, CPU, disk usage
Monitor device status and health

slides.title: SNMP Protocols
slides.body:
SNMP Messages
Message Type
Direction
GetRequest
Manager → Agent
GetNextRequest
Manager → Agent
Purpose
Manager asks for a specific value (e.g., "What is the CPU usage?")
Manager asks for the next value in the MIB tree (used for walking through MIB entries sequentially)
SetRequest
Manager → Agent
Manager changes/sets a value on the agent (e.g., "Set the interface status to UP")

slides.title: SNMP Protocols
slides.body:
SNMP Messages
Message Type
Direction
GetResponse
Agent → Manager
Purpose
Agent sends back the requested value as a response to Get/Set requests
Trap
Agent → Manager
Agent sends an unsolicited alert to the Manager when a critical event occurs (e.g., link down, high CPU) — No acknowledgement from Manager

slides.title: SNMP Protocols
slides.body:
SNMP Versions - v1, v2c, v3
SNMPv1
First version of SNMP
Uses a shared password called Community String
Password sent in plain text anyone can read it
Not Secure

slides.title: SNMP Protocols
slides.body:
SNMP Versions - v1, v2c, v3
SNMPv2c
"c" stands for community-based
Still sends password in plain text
Added new useful messages: GetBulk and Inform
Better performance for large networks
Faster, but still not secure

slides.title: SNMP Protocols
slides.body:
SNMP Versions - v1, v2c, v3
SNMPv3
Provides proper authentication (verifies identity)
Provides encryption (scrambles data similar to what we learned in TLS/HTTPS in S6)
Controls who can access what on each device
Secure, Recommended for use

slides.title: SNMP Versions - v1, v2c, v3
slides.body:
